Service: Total shoulder replacement, CPT 23472
Surgeon: Reyes, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Appeals Department:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for total shoulder replacement (CPT 23472), as stated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-18. This appeal is submitted well within the 180-day deadline stated on that notice (by 2027-02-14).

Stated Reason for Denial

The notice states: "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery."

I disagree with this determination. The medical record already in the plan's possession documents an extensive, well-supervised, and unsuccessful course of conservative treatment, as detailed below.

Clinical Facts Documenting Conservative Treatment

1. Duration of symptoms: I have had progressive shoulder pain for 24 months, unrelieved by rest.

2. Supervised physical therapy: I completed 16 visits of supervised physical therapy focused on range of motion and periscapular strengthening over 14 weeks, from 2026-04-12 to 2026-07-19, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note.

3. Medication trial: I used NSAIDs for 6 months without adequate relief.

4. Injection trial: I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-07, which gave only 4 weeks of partial relief.

5. Imaging findings: Shoulder radiographs (true AP and axillary views) obtained 2026-06-04 show complete loss of glenohumeral joint space with osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, and a flattened glenoid. CT confirms an intact rotator cuff.

6. Functional loss: I cannot reach overhead, dress without help, or sleep on the affected side.

7. Exam findings: Glenohumeral crepitus, active forward elevation limited to 90 degrees, external rotation limited to 10 degrees, with intact cuff strength.

8. No disqualifying comorbidities: No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker.

Mapping These Facts to the Applicable Clinical Guideline

Based on my research, Iowa Total Care/Ambetter delegates medical-necessity review of shoulder surgery, including CPT 23472, to its vendor Evolent, whose criteria for this procedure appear in a document titled "Shoulder Arthroplasty" (Evolent Clinical Guideline 1769). I was able to retrieve a publicly posted copy of this guideline. I want to be transparent that I cannot confirm this retrieved copy is word-for-word identical to whatever version the plan's reviewer actually applied to my case; I am therefore also formally requesting, as part of this appeal, that the plan identify and provide me with the specific policy, guideline number, and version/effective date actually used to deny my request, per my appeal rights.

With that caveat, the retrieved text of Evolent Clinical Guideline 1769 states, under the general requirements for shoulder surgery, that clinical notes should address:

"Symptom onset, duration, and severity ... Loss of function and/or limitations ... Type and duration of non-operative management modalities"

My records address each of these elements, as summarized above.

The same guideline's criteria for Total Shoulder Arthroplasty include:

"Evidence of painful osteoarthritis or inflammatory, non-infectious arthritis (e.g., rheumatoid) with functional limitations such as ADLs, employment, or recreation"

"Functional and intact rotator cuff and deltoid (adequate abduction strength); confirmed by physical examination, MRI, or CT scan"

"Complete or near-complete loss of joint space* on axillary or AP X-rays (internal rotation and/or external rotation)*"
with the accompanying note: "In those with bone-on-bone articulation on axillary or true AP X-rays, non-operative treatment is not required."

"Failure of at least 12 weeks of non-operative treatment that includes at least ONE of the following:
○ Physical therapy or properly instructed home exercise program
○ Rest or activity modification
○ Application of heat or ice
○ Pharmacologic treatment (oral/topical NSAIDS, acetaminophen, analgesics)
○ Corticosteroid injections"

My records satisfy every one of these elements, and in fact exceed them:

- My imaging shows "complete... loss of joint space" with bone-on-bone changes, which the guideline's own note states means "non-operative treatment is not required" at all.
- Even though non-operative treatment was not strictly required given the bone-on-bone imaging findings, I nonetheless completed 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy (16 visits) — exceeding the "at least 12 weeks" benchmark — plus 6 months of NSAIDs and a corticosteroid injection, satisfying more than the "at least ONE" modality the guideline requires.
- My CT and physical examination confirm an intact rotator cuff and intact cuff strength, satisfying the "functional and intact rotator cuff and deltoid" criterion.
- My functional limitations (inability to reach overhead, dress independently, or sleep on the affected side) and exam findings (forward elevation limited to 90°, external rotation limited to 10°) document the required functional limitation and loss of function.

I also note that the same guideline lists as a contraindication: "Any cortisone injection into the joint within 12 weeks of surgery." My corticosteroid injection was administered 2026-06-07. To ensure this criterion is unambiguously satisfied, I ask that surgery be scheduled no earlier than 12 weeks after that date, and I ask the plan to confirm that this timing is acceptable so that this issue cannot become a basis for a further denial.

Requested Action

Based on the clinical record — which documents 24 months of symptoms, 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy, 6 months of NSAID therapy, a corticosteroid injection, and imaging showing complete loss of joint space with an intact rotator cuff — I am requesting that the plan reverse the denial of CPT 23472 and approve the total shoulder replacement recommended by Dr. Reyes.

I am also requesting, in writing, the specific policy or guideline document (with title, number, and effective date) that the reviewer actually relied upon to determine that my conservative-treatment trial was inadequate, along with the completed clinical review checklist or worksheet used in the initial determination, so that I and my surgeon can respond to any additional specific deficiency the plan believes remains.

Enclosed / Available on Request

- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-12 to 2026-07-19, 16 visits)
- Medication and injection records (NSAID trial; corticosteroid injection 2026-06-07)
- Shoulder radiographs and CT report, dated 2026-06-04
- Office notes documenting exam findings and functional limitations
- Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Reyes [to be provided/enclosed]

Please contact me at [phone number] or my provider's office at [provider phone/fax] if any additional information is needed. I request written confirmation of receipt of this appeal and a decision within the timeframe required for ACA marketplace plan appeals.

Sincerely,

Reese Carter
